shot_description: A blue lightning arrowhead and a gold sun-fire arrowhead meet point to point in the center of a black frame and burst.
camera_plan: Extreme close-up, locked off, then a 6-frame snap zoom out

shot_description: Two chariots face each other across a cleared ring of red earth while two halted armies watch.
camera_plan: Extreme wide, 24mm, eye level, slow push-in

shot_description: Karna touches his bow to his forehead, then his eyes lift to screen left.
camera_plan: Medium close-up, 85mm, slight low angle, slow push-in

shot_description: Arjuna draws Gandiva and blue static crawls up the bow.
camera_plan: Medium close-up, 85mm, mirror of A03, slow push-in

shot_description: Krishna flicks the reins and the white horses surge forward.
camera_plan: Low tracking shot at wheel height, 18mm, fast dolly

shot_description: Karna looses a fan of seven arrows in one draw.
camera_plan: Arrow-cam: camera launches with the arrows, 35mm, then whip-pan

shot_description: Arjuna's arrows split Karna's arrows in mid-air, one by one.
camera_plan: Medium wide, 35mm, camera shake on each hit

shot_description: The sky fills with so many arrows that they blot out the sun.
camera_plan: Crane up from ground to high top-down, 24mm

shot_description: In the arrow-darkness the two warriors, exhausted, look at each other.
camera_plan: Split-screen two-shot, both 85mm close-ups, locked off

shot_description: Karna draws a single arrow from a golden quiver; its head is a serpent's mouth and its eye opens.
camera_plan: Macro insert, 100mm, rack focus

shot_description: Karna draws the snake arrow to his ear and meteors fall from a red sky.
camera_plan: Low angle, 24mm, 90-degree orbit

shot_description: The snake arrow tears across the sky, splitting it with a line of fire.
camera_plan: Wide, 24mm, whip-pan following the arrow

shot_description: Krishna presses his foot down and the chariot sinks a cubit into the earth; the horses kneel.
camera_plan: Low angle on the chariot floor, 18mm, then a hard drop

shot_description: The snake arrow strikes Arjuna's crown off instead of his head.
camera_plan: Medium close-up, 50mm, speed ramp 100 to 10 to 100 percent

shot_description: Arjuna rises bare-headed, pushes his loose hair back from his face and lifts Gandiva again.
camera_plan: Medium close-up, 85mm, slow push-in

shot_description: Karna's left wheel sinks; he leaps down and heaves it, and the whole earth lifts a little.
camera_plan: Low wide, 18mm, the horizon tilts

shot_description: Karna raises a palm to ask Arjuna to wait; Krishna's look answers with a memory of Abhimanyu.
camera_plan: Over-the-shoulder from Arjuna to Karna, 50mm, one 12-frame insert

shot_description: Arjuna's razor arrow cuts Karna's gold banner and it falls across the sun.
camera_plan: Wide, 35mm, slow tilt down

shot_description: Arjuna draws the Anjalika and rings of lightning ripple out from Gandiva.
camera_plan: Wide to extreme close-up, one continuous push, 24mm to 135mm feel

shot_description: The Anjalika flies; Karna's silhouette stands against the sun as the sun goes dark.
camera_plan: Impact frames, then a locked wide silhouette

shot_description: A column of light rises from where Karna fell and enters the sun.
camera_plan: Wide, 24mm, crane up

shot_description: Arjuna lowers Gandiva and does not celebrate; Krishna watches the light.
camera_plan: Medium wide, 50mm, locked off, hold the final pose

shot_description: In a quiet forest hermitage at dawn, @vyasa sits still before the sacred fire, holding the entire epic in his mind.
camera_plan: Extreme wide, 24mm, slow push-in toward the thatched hut

shot_description: @vyasa opens his eyes, wondering who on earth can write down the vast poem he has composed.
camera_plan: Medium close-up, 85mm, locked off

shot_description: The four-faced @brahma appears in soft golden light above a lotus seat; @vyasa rises with joined palms, bows, and walks around him.
camera_plan: Locked symmetrical wide, 35mm, zero camera movement

shot_description: @vyasa speaks of all his poem contains—stars, oceans, dharma, and war—and says no writer exists on earth.
camera_plan: Medium two-shot dissolving into three 1.5s painted cosmic flashes, then back

shot_description: @brahma names Vyasa's work a true poem and counsels him: 'Think of Ganesa to write it,' then vanishes in light.
camera_plan: Locked symmetrical medium shot on @brahma, 50mm

shot_description: @vyasa closes his eyes and calls @ganesha in thought; @ganesha appears before him and sits ready to write.
camera_plan: Locked symmetrical wide, 35mm, balanced left-right framing

shot_description: @ganesha states his condition that his pen never stop; @vyasa answers that he must not write what he has not understood. @ganesha says 'Om'.
camera_plan: Over-the-shoulder two-shot alternating, 50mm

shot_description: The stylus glides rapidly across incised palm-leaf strips, etching Sanskrit lines without pause as leaves stack up.
camera_plan: Macro insert on palm leaf and stylus, 100mm, tracking along the line

shot_description: His pen failing mid-verse, @ganesha immediately snaps off his right tusk and writes on without missing a beat.
camera_plan: Locked symmetrical medium frame, 50mm, 2-frame white-gold impact flash on the snap

shot_description: @vyasa knits a dense verse; even the omniscient @ganesha pauses briefly to ponder it while @vyasa composes ahead with a quiet smile.
camera_plan: Medium wide two-shot, 50mm, gentle slow push-in

shot_description: Over the first verses of the Bharata, the light of the sacred fire swells like a lamp dispelling darkness across the earth.
camera_plan: Crane up from the palm-leaf firelight into warm golden radiance

shot_description: The golden lamp flame settles at center as the darkness clears; the title card 'THE SCRIBE' fades in over the glow.
camera_plan: Locked off, hold to final frame

shot_description: King @dushmanta rides at the head of a vast royal army — chariots, elephants, horses, foot soldiers — sweeping into a dense forest.
camera_plan: Extreme wide, 24mm, low angle, slow pull-back as army flows past

shot_description: The hunt empties the forest: deer scatter in all directions, birds burst from the canopy, the earth trembles under a thousand chariots.
camera_plan: Medium wide, 50mm, handheld energy, quick pan left-to-right

shot_description: Alone with only his minister and priest, @dushmanta reaches the river Malini: clear water over white stones, forest flowers on the bank, the sound of the hermitage's sacred fire.
camera_plan: Wide, 35mm, slow push toward river bank

shot_description: @dushmanta walks through the hermitage gate into Kanwa's forest retreat, leaving his weapons at the threshold.
camera_plan: Medium, 50mm, locked, then slow push through the gate

shot_description: @dushmanta looks around Kanwa's hermitage and finds it empty: fire burning, palm leaves set out, but no sage.
camera_plan: Slow wide pan, 35mm, left to right across the empty hermitage

shot_description: @shakuntala comes out from behind a flowering tree, greets @dushmanta with the proper hermitage welcome, and says her father Kanwa has gone to gather fruit.
camera_plan: Medium, 50mm, locked two-shot; she enters frame from behind a flowering tree

shot_description: @dushmanta is struck by @shakuntala's beauty and composure; he looks at her with quiet wonder.
camera_plan: Close-up on @dushmanta, 85mm, locked

shot_description: @dushmanta asks @shakuntala who she is and whose daughter. She answers openly: Kanwa the sage is her father, though she was born of Viswamitra and the apsara Menaka.
camera_plan: Medium two-shot, 50mm, slight push-in

shot_description: Painted flashback: Viswamitra's blazing tapas on a mountain peak; Indra watches in fear from his throne and sends the apsara Menaka to break the penance; Menaka is born into the air above a river bank and lays her baby daughter on the warm grass before vanishing.
camera_plan: Painterly flash series: three painted panels, 2.4s each

shot_description: @shakuntala finishes her story calmly, unashamed of her parentage — a great sage's daughter and an apsara's child, raised in the hermitage.
camera_plan: Medium close-up on @shakuntala, 85mm, locked

shot_description: A ring of great vultures sits motionless in the tall trees above the Malini riverbank, watching over the sleeping infant girl left by Menaka.
camera_plan: Crane down from canopy to riverbank, 35mm

shot_description: The sage @kanwa comes down to the river to draw water, sees the infant, and lifts her with great tenderness.
camera_plan: Medium wide, 50mm, locked

shot_description: @kanwa names her Shakuntala — she who was guarded by the shakunta birds — and decides to raise her as his own daughter.
camera_plan: Close-up insert on @kanwa's face, 85mm, then cut to baby’s face

shot_description: @dushmanta asks @shakuntala to marry him in the Gandharva form, man and woman by their own free choice, without priest or fire.
camera_plan: Medium two-shot, 50mm, slight push-in

shot_description: @shakuntala agrees — but only on one condition: their son must be named @dushmanta's heir and king after him. She speaks it plainly, without apology.
camera_plan: Medium close-up on @shakuntala, 85mm, locked

shot_description: @dushmanta agrees to @shakuntala's condition immediately — the first son born of her shall be king.
camera_plan: Medium close-up on @dushmanta, 85mm, locked

shot_description: @kanwa returns from the forest, knows everything through his sight, and blesses them both. @dushmanta departs for his capital shortly after.
camera_plan: Wide three-shot, 35mm, locked symmetrical

shot_description: Six years later: a fearless boy — Sarvadamana — rides a full-grown lion around the hermitage, binding tigers to the trees and opening their mouths to count their teeth.
camera_plan: Low wide, 24mm, handheld energy tracking shot

shot_description: The sages name the boy Bharata — the subduer of all, the one who will give his name to a nation. @kanwa tells @shakuntala it is time to take him to his father's court.
camera_plan: Medium wide, 50mm, locked

shot_description: @shakuntala and young Bharata walk together away from the hermitage along a forest road toward the distant capital.
camera_plan: Wide, 35mm, slow push-in from behind them

shot_description: @shakuntala presents her son in @dushmanta's court. @dushmanta looks at her and denies all knowledge of her — he says he does not remember her and questions her birth.
camera_plan: Wide court shot, 35mm; then close-up on @dushmanta, 85mm

shot_description: @shakuntala answers @dushmanta's denial with her great speech on truth: a mother is a river, a father is the ocean; a man who abandons wife and child abandons dharma itself. Four lines from the Ganguli text, chosen by sai: lines 1, 3, 7 and 10.
camera_plan: Medium close-up on @shakuntala, 85mm, locked; slight push-in over the speech
notes: Grade S (twist) | Lines 9150-9279 (four lines: 1, 3, 7, 10 — see shakuntala_lines.md) (dramatised)

shot_description: @dushmanta listens without expression as @shakuntala finishes. He does not move. The court waits.
camera_plan: Medium close-up on @dushmanta, 85mm, locked

shot_description: @shakuntala lifts her son's hand and turns to leave the court with her dignity intact. She does not weep. She does not look back.
camera_plan: Wide court shot, 35mm, locked; she moves toward the door

shot_description: As @shakuntala reaches the door, a voice from the sky fills the hall and declares: Bharata is @dushmanta's son. The king must acknowledge him. The court turns upward in awe.
camera_plan: Wide court, 35mm, then slow crane up to ceiling as the voice sounds

shot_description: @dushmanta speaks openly to his court: he knew all along, but waited for heaven to confirm it so the people would hear the truth from the voice of the gods, not from him alone.
camera_plan: Medium wide three-shot, 50mm, locked

shot_description: @dushmanta installs Bharata as crown prince. The boy stands before the throne for the first time as the heir of the Puru line.
camera_plan: Wide symmetrical court shot, 35mm, locked

shot_description: @vyasa's voice over the court image: 'This is the line that ends with the Kurus.' Match-cut back to the hermitage: Vyasa dictating, Ganesha writing, the lamp burning. Pull back to the forest. Cut to black.
camera_plan: Match cut back to hermitage; slow pull-back from @vyasa dictating; then wide hold
